facts.raw_span: bilateral ventriculomegaly with dilation of both frontal and occipital horns
multiple hyperechoic regions with indistinct margins within the ventricular lumens
areas of high signal intensity on T1-weighted images and low signal intensity on T2-weighted images within the ventricles

a comprehensive workup—including a TORCH panel, platelet count, prothrombin time, partial thromboplastin time, plasminogen levels, von Willebrand factor, factor V Leiden, protein S, protein C, and antiplatelet antibodies—returned within normal limits

concepts.why: Bilateral ventriculomegaly and ventricular enlargement are indicative of congenital hydrocephalus.
Bilateral ventriculomegaly with irregular ventricular walls and hyperechoic regions suggests fetal ventriculomegaly.
A comprehensive workup including a TORCH panel returned within normal limits, but the presence of ventriculomegaly and irregular ventricular walls could suggest an intrauterine infection.
A comprehensive workup including coagulation studies returned within normal limits, but the presence of ventriculomegaly and irregular ventricular walls could suggest a fetal coagulopathy.
Bilateral ventriculomegaly and a roughened-appearing choroid plexus are indicative of a congenital CNS anomaly.
It explains the areas of high signal intensity on T1-weighted images and low signal intensity on T2-weighted images within the ventricles.

rationales.F05: Bilateral ventriculomegaly is a key feature of Congenital Hydrocephalus and Fetal Ventriculomegaly.
rationales.F07: Multiple hyperechoic regions within the ventricular lumens may indicate intraventricular hemorrhage.
rationales.F10: Bilateral ventricular enlargement is a characteristic finding in Congenital Hydrocephalus and Fetal Ventriculomegaly.
rationales.F11: Areas of high signal intensity on T1-weighted images and low signal intensity on T2-weighted images within the ventricles may indicate hemorrhage or other pathology.
rationales.F12: A comprehensive workup with normal results helps rule out Intrauterine Infection, Fetal Coagulopathy, and Fetal Intraventricular Hemorrhage.

frontier_selector.rationale: bilateral ventriculomegaly with dilation of both frontal and occipital horns and irregular ventricular walls support Fetal Ventriculomegaly, which is a more specific diagnosis than Congenital Hydrocephalus in this context
